accountantMode.label: Accountant Mode
accountantMode.toggleTitle: Tap to change — an explanation appears before anything is applied
accountantMode.turnOffMessage: Accountant Mode is currently ON. Turning it off hides the accounting menus — Transaction Records (journal), Details by Account (general ledger), Chart of Accounts — and the debit/credit labels on forms, so the screen speaks everyday language only (money in / money out). This changes only YOUR view: not the data, the figures, or your access rights. You can turn it back on at any time.
accountantMode.turnOnMessage: Accountant Mode is currently OFF. Turning it on shows the accounting menus — Transaction Records (journal), Details by Account (general ledger), Chart of Accounts — and the debit/credit labels on forms. Useful if you know bookkeeping. This changes only YOUR view: not the data, the figures, or your access rights. You can turn it off again at any time.

contracts.emptyLinesTitle: This contract has no item lines yet

contracts.unmatchedDelivery: Some document lines name goods that are not on this contract — delivery orders {delivered} kg. Those lines do not count towards fulfilling the contract.
contracts.unmatchedInvoice: Some document lines name goods that are not on this contract — invoices {invoiced} kg. Those lines do not count towards fulfilling the contract.

invoices.createDescriptionBefore: Type it in by hand, or pull it ("Ambil") from a contract so the goods, remaining quantities, and prices fill themselves in. Once saved, the balance shows up under “Unpaid by Customers” until it is settled. First time? The guided flow is easier:
invoices.pullDescriptionA: Pick the source contract, then pull its goods across. What comes over is the

invoices.noContractLines: This contract has no item lines yet.

invoices.lineRemainingOver: Contract remainder {kg} kg — over the remainder, the invoice will be rejected!

sales.title: Record a Sale
sales.descriptionA: Guided step by step: customer, goods, shipment, then the invoice. Move back and forth as you like —
sales.descriptionB: until you press “Finish & Save” on the last step.
sales.savedHint: Every document below was created together in a single save.
sales.outstandingLoadFailed: The contract remainder failed to load. You can still enter the goods by hand.
sales.saveFailed: The sale could not be saved yet.
sales.pullNoneContract: Every item on this contract has already been invoiced.
sales.pullNote: {count} lines pulled from the remainder of contract {contractNo}. Quantities may be reduced, never raised above the remainder.
sales.pullDescription: If this sale bills an existing contract, pick it here: the goods, remaining quantities, and prices fill themselves in, and the invoice cannot exceed the contract remainder.
sales.lineNoStockItem: This item is not in the stock list, so no delivery order can be issued for it. The invoice can still be raised.
sales.lineStockAndRemaining: Stock available {stock} kg · contract remainder {remaining} kg
sales.lineStockAndRemainingOver: Stock available {stock} kg · contract remainder {remaining} kg — over the contract remainder!
sales.shipCheckboxA: The goods have shipped — issue a
sales.shipCheckboxHint: A delivery order reduces stock and posts the cost-of-goods journal. If nothing has left yet, leave this unticked and carry on — the delivery order can be issued later.
sales.emptyStockDescription: A delivery order reduces stock, so the goods must be recorded first.
sales.shipStockOverStock: Stock available {stock} kg — over stock, the delivery order will be rejected!
sales.shipStockOverOrder: Stock available {stock} kg — more than the quantity ordered!
sales.shipStockOverBoth: Stock available {stock} kg — over stock, the delivery order will be rejected! — more than the quantity ordered!
sales.deliveryAdvancedDescription: Vehicle number, container number, and shipping notes.
sales.billedHint: Quantities are pulled from the previous steps, not retyped. Reduce them if only part is being billed now.
sales.invoiceAdvancedDescription: Due date, currency & rate, and VAT. An ordinary rupiah invoice uses the defaults and need not open this.
sales.deliveryHint: Dated {date} — stock is reduced and the cost-of-goods journal is posted.
sales.summaryFooter: Once saved, the unpaid balance appears under “Unpaid by Customers”. If the amount reaches the approval threshold, the invoice is saved but its journal is held until approved.

purchases.title: Record a Purchase
purchases.descriptionA: Guided step by step: supplier, goods, goods into the warehouse, then recording what you owe. Move back and forth as you like —
purchases.descriptionB: until you press “Finish & Save” on the last step.
purchases.learnMore: Learn about this: what a purchase is
purchases.savedHint: Everything was recorded together in a single save.
purchases.saveFailed: The purchase could not be saved yet.
purchases.goodsHintA: Quantity × purchase price here becomes the purchase value recorded as a
purchases.lineNotInStock: This item is not in the stock list yet, so it cannot be booked into the warehouse. Its purchase value is still recorded.
purchases.receiptCheckboxA: The goods have reached the warehouse — add them to
purchases.receiptHintA: Stock goes up together with its cost, which is later used to work out
purchases.receiptHintB: when the goods are sold. No extra journal — inventory already came in through the purchase journal.
purchases.overReceive: The quantity received exceeds the quantity bought.
purchases.fxCostHint: Stock cost is always recorded in rupiah, so the {currency} purchase price is multiplied by the rate you enter in the next step. Fill in that rate first if you have not.

purchases.advancedDescription: Currency & rate, input VAT, and the purchase note.
purchases.inputVatHint: Posted separately to the input VAT account. Enter 0 if there is none.
purchases.noteHint: The item details from step 2 are carried into this note automatically, because a purchase is stored as a single amount.
purchases.receiptSummaryHint: Dated {date} — stock goes up, with no extra journal.

deliveryOrders.title: Delivery Orders
deliveryOrders.description: The document that ships goods. Issuing one reduces stock and recognises the cost of the goods that leave.
deliveryOrders.stockNoteB: (bags × kg/bag) when the delivery order is issued. Issuing is refused when stock is short.
deliveryOrders.emptyDescription: Create a delivery order to ship goods and reduce stock.
deliveryOrders.createDescription: Pick the consignee and (optionally) a source document, then set the goods and quantities (bags × kg/bag). Issuing the delivery order reduces stock in kilograms.
deliveryOrders.learnMore: Learn about this: what a delivery order is
deliveryOrders.noItems: Add at least one item before issuing the delivery order.
deliveryOrders.submitFailed: The delivery order could not be issued yet.
deliveryOrders.emptyStockDescription: A delivery order reduces stock, so the goods must already be on record. Record your first goods-in.
deliveryOrders.lineAvailableOver: Available {stock} {unit} — over stock, the delivery order will be rejected!
deliveryOrders.linePickItem: Pick an item to see its stock

returns.title: Returns
returns.description: Goods sent back — reversing part of an invoice or purchase along with its stock, receivable/payable, and VAT.
returns.noteA: A return is valued at the
returns.noteB: and may never exceed the quantity or value still outstanding. A sales return puts stock back in; a purchase return takes stock out.
returns.emptyDescription: Record goods sent back from an invoice or a purchase here.
returns.createDescription: Pick the original document, then set the goods and quantities being returned. Value and VAT follow the original document and may not exceed what is still returnable.
returns.fillOneLine: Enter a return quantity on at least one line.
returns.fillOneItem: Enter at least one line of returned goods.
returns.saved: The return is saved and journalled.
returns.networkFailed: Could not reach the server. Please try again.
returns.typeSales: Sales Return (goods back from a customer)
returns.typePurchase: Purchase Return (goods sent back to a supplier)
returns.effectSuffix: Valued at the rate of the original document.

suppliers.txEffectPayment: Reduces Accounts Payable and the cash balance

suppliers.txAllocHintA: Pick the purchases this transaction pays. Left empty, the balance per document is merely

journal.emptyDescription: Most journal entries are created automatically from invoices, contracts, cash, and stock. Manual entries are for corrections and adjustments.

periods.title: Close Period
periods.description: Closing a month locks every transaction dated in that month — none can be created, changed, or deleted — so reports you have already issued do not quietly change afterwards. Review the summary before locking.

periods.closeNotePlaceholder: Example: already reconciled with the bank statement

finance.headingDefaultDesc: Record money in or money out, together with its category.
finance.errNeedOneAccountant: Fill in one of them: Money In (debit) or Money Out (credit). One of the two must be greater than 0.
finance.errNeedOnePlain: Fill in one of them: Money In or Money Out. One of the two must be greater than 0.
finance.errBothSides: One transaction may only go one way: fill in Money In only, or Money Out only. If money really moves between cash accounts, record two separate transactions.
finance.errPickCounterAccount: Select a counter account — the automatic journal entry needs the other side of the transaction.
finance.errPickCategory: Select a category — where this money came from, or what it was used for.
finance.errRateRequired: A rate is required for a {currency} transaction: without it, the rupiah value in the ledger cannot be computed.
finance.saveFailed: The transaction could not be saved yet.
finance.counterHintAccountant: The other side of the automatic journal entry: where this money came from, or what it was used for (e.g.
finance.counterHintPlain: Where this money came from, or what it was used for (e.g.
finance.journalPreviewNote: The journal entry is created automatically when the transaction is saved. Figures are in {currency}.
finance.advancedDescription: A currency other than rupiah (with its rate) and an extra note. An ordinary rupiah transaction never needs to open this.
finance.rateHint: Required for a foreign currency — the IDR value in the ledger is computed from this rate.

reconciliation.title: Match Bank Statement
reconciliation.description: Match the internal cash/bank book against the bank statement, period by period.
reconciliation.emptyDescription: Create the first reconciliation: pick the bank account, the period, and the opening/closing balance from the statement.
reconciliation.newDescription: Take the opening and closing balance from the bank statement for the period being reconciled.
reconciliation.oneAccountHint: One account = one currency. The reconciliation only compares figures in this currency.
reconciliation.summaryComplete: Done — every transaction is matched and the difference is 0.
reconciliation.summaryIncomplete: Not done yet — {book} book transactions and {statement} statement lines are still unmatched.
reconciliation.amountsDiffer: The amounts differ ({book} vs {statement}) — they cannot be matched.
reconciliation.csvHintTail: . Amounts are plain numbers; positive means money in.

fixedAssets.title: Fixed Assets
fixedAssets.descriptionBefore: Vehicles, equipment, and buildings, together with their depreciation. Book value and depreciation expense flow automatically into the Balance Sheet and Income Statement.
fixedAssets.noCategoryDescription: A category sets the method, the useful life, and the asset/accumulated/expense accounts every asset in it uses.
fixedAssets.emptyDescription: Register a vehicle, a piece of equipment, or a building so its depreciation is computed automatically.
fixedAssets.footnoteBefore: Straight-line depreciation is run monthly and posted as
fixedAssets.footnoteEntry: Dr: Depreciation Expense / Cr: Accumulated Depreciation
fixedAssets.footnoteAfter: . Re-running a month that has already been posted does not duplicate the entry.
fixedAssets.runNothing: No asset needs depreciating for this period.
fixedAssets.networkFailed: Could not reach the server. Please try again.
fixedAssets.categoriesDescription: A category sets the method, the useful life, and the asset/accumulated/expense accounts every asset in it uses. A new asset copies these values and may override them.
fixedAssets.emptyCategoryDescription: Create the first category above — for example Vehicles, Equipment, or Buildings.
fixedAssets.byLocationDescription: Active assets grouped by location. Figures in IDR.
fixedAssets.emptyActiveDescription: Register assets and fill in their location to see the per-location recap.
fixedAssets.noCategoryFormDescription: Every asset must belong to a category, which sets its method, useful life, and accounts.
fixedAssets.newDescriptionBefore: A vehicle, a piece of equipment, or a building that will be depreciated automatically.
fixedAssets.assetNamePlaceholder: e.g. Colt Diesel truck B 1234 XY
fixedAssets.noJournalMiddle: create a journal entry — the acquisition cost has usually been recorded already through a purchase or a cash entry. What does post is
fixedAssets.noDepreciation: No depreciation has been posted yet.
fixedAssets.moveHint: Records the move — no journal entry is created.
fixedAssets.moveSaved: The asset's location has been updated.
fixedAssets.disposeHint: Removes the asset's value and its accumulated depreciation, records the proceeds, and journalises the gain or loss on disposal.
fixedAssets.disposeSaved: The disposal has been recorded and journalised.

dashboard.description: Stock, cash, and sales at a glance for {name}
dashboard.plainDescription: The key figures without accounting jargon. All amounts in IDR (the ledger base value) and every one can be checked in its source report.
dashboard.moneyInExplanation: All income booked this month, for example sales to customers.
dashboard.moneyOutExplanation: All costs and expenses booked this month.
dashboard.profitLossExplanation: Money in minus money out this month — a plus figure means profit, a minus figure means loss.
dashboard.receivablesExplanation: Outstanding amounts on invoices and contracts your customers have not settled yet.
dashboard.payablesExplanation: Outstanding amounts on purchases you have not yet paid your suppliers.
dashboard.overdueBills: {count} bills are past their due date.
dashboard.stockDescription: Low stock = {threshold} units or fewer left
dashboard.chartStockConditionDesc: Items grouped by how much stock is left
dashboard.chartTopStockDesc: The largest stock balances right now (up to 8 items)
dashboard.emptyMovementsDescription: Every item received and issued shows up here. Record your first one.
dashboard.financeDescription: Balances and money movement over the last 6 months, per currency
dashboard.contractsDescription: Sales activity and the deals currently running
dashboard.emptyContractsDescription: A contract starts the document chain: delivery orders, invoices, and payments all follow from it.

inventory.uncostedNote: {count} items have no incoming cost yet — they are not included in the total.
inventory.updateDescription: Record goods coming into or going out of the warehouse.
inventory.learnMoreCogs: Learn this: the cost of goods sold
inventory.itemSaveFailed: The new item could not be saved yet.
inventory.movementSaveFailed: The stock movement could not be saved yet.
inventory.pickItemFirst: Pick an item first — a stock movement always belongs to one item.
inventory.qtyPositive: Quantity must be greater than 0 — a zero movement changes nothing.
inventory.emptyFormDescription: Create your first item with the “+ New Item” button above, then record its incoming stock.
inventory.overStockWarning: More than the stock available ({qty} {unit}). Stock may never go negative, so this movement will be rejected.
inventory.unitCostHint: Required. Used to compute COGS (weighted average) when goods go out — without it, profit is recorded too high.
inventory.cogsAutoHint: COGS is computed automatically from the average cost of incoming goods, then posted to the journal (Dr: Cost of Goods Sold / Cr: Inventory).
inventory.opnameDescription: Physical count against the system records · low stock is {threshold} units or fewer
inventory.opnameEmptyDescription: A stock count compares the records with a physical count. Record your first goods receipt so there is something to compare.
inventory.opnameHint: Enter the physical quantity you counted. Items left blank are not changed.
inventory.varianceCount: {count} items with a variance will be adjusted (journalled to Inventory Variance).
inventory.opnameConfirmMessage: {count} items will be adjusted on {date}. Each variance creates a stock movement and a journal entry to the Inventory Variance account, valued at average cost. This cannot be undone automatically — correct it with the next stock count if it is wrong.
inventory.opnameFailed: The stock count could not be saved. Please try again.

setup.title: Company Setup
setup.doneNote: The company is already set up. The wizard runs only once — below is a summary of the opening balances on record.
setup.reflectedBefore: These opening balances already appear in the
setup.wizardDescription: Start the books from the right position. This step runs only once.
setup.npwpPlaceholder: Optional — can be filled in later
setup.ledgerNoteAfter: as the base currency. The opening journal is dated at the start of the fiscal year, before the first transaction.
setup.coaNoteBefore: The standard chart of accounts (trading/export) is ready:
setup.coaNoteAfter: active accounts. The opening balances in the next step will use these accounts.
setup.coaHint: You can review or adjust the accounts in the Chart of Accounts menu at any time.
setup.cashSectionHint: Cash and bank account balances as at the start of the fiscal year.
setup.cashEmpty: There is no cash/bank account in the COA yet.
setup.receivablesHint: Amounts still to be collected from each customer.
setup.inventoryHint: Value of merchandise inventory (IDR) as at the start of the fiscal year.
setup.payablesHint: Amounts still owed to each supplier.
setup.saveNoteAfter: that balances, and marks the company as set up. This step cannot be repeated.
setup.errNoBalance: Enter at least one opening balance (cash/bank, receivable, payable, or inventory).
setup.errUnrated: There is a foreign-currency balance without a rate. Enter the rate so the IDR value is not wrong.
setup.errSaveFailed: The opening balances could not be saved.
setup.errNetwork: Could not reach the server. Please try again.
setup.toastDone: Setup complete. The opening journal is saved and balanced.
setup.unratedWarning: {count} foreign-currency balances have no rate yet — enter the rate before saving.

approvalMessage.approved: {document} approved and already posted to the journal.
approvalMessage.rejected: {document} rejected — not posted to the journal.

approvals.descriptionBefore: A transaction that reaches the approval threshold is saved first, but
approvals.descriptionStrong: is not yet posted to the journal
approvals.descriptionAfter: . Once approved, its journal is issued immediately; if rejected, the document stays saved without a journal and can be corrected and resubmitted.
approvals.inboxEmpty: No documents are waiting for your approval.
approvals.inboxEmptyHint: Thresholds and approver roles are configured in
approvals.decisionNotePlaceholder: Example: the price matches the master contract
approvals.decisionNoteHint: Required (at least 5 characters) when rejecting. Every decision is written to the audit log.
approvals.approveMessage: Once approved, its journal is issued immediately and recorded in the ledger. Undoing it later must be done with a reversing entry, not by deleting.
approvals.rejectMessage: The document stays saved but is not posted to the journal. The requester sees your reason and can correct it and resubmit.
approvals.mineEmpty: None of your documents need approval yet.
approvals.errDecision: The decision could not be saved.
approvals.approvedWithJournal: Approved — its journal has been issued.
approvals.approvedNoJournal: Approved. This document produces no journal (zero value/cancelled).
approvals.rejectedToast: Rejected. The document stays saved without a journal.
approvals.errMarkRead: Could not mark it as read.
approvals.rulesDescA: Set the value at which a contract, invoice, or payment must be approved, and who approves it. The threshold is compared with the document's
approvals.rulesDescB: value (a foreign-currency document is converted first at its own rate) and is
approvals.rulesDescC: — a value exactly equal to the threshold still needs approval. A new rule only applies to documents created after it.
approvals.rulesEmptyTitle: No rules yet — every transaction is posted to the journal straight away, as usual.
approvals.rulesEmptyHint: Add your first rule in the form beside this to start screening large-value transactions.
approvals.deactivateMessage: New documents will no longer be matched against this rule. Requests already raised stay on record and still have to be decided.
approvals.paymentHint: “Payment” covers invoice settlements, contract settlements, and payments to suppliers.
approvals.minAmountHint: Inclusive: a document worth exactly this amount still needs approval. If several rules match, the highest threshold reached is the one that applies.
approvals.errSaveRule: The rule could not be saved.
approvals.errDeactivate: The rule could not be deactivated.
